title: Spinal fusion
what: The surgeon joins two or more vertebrae with screws and rods, sometimes placing a spacer between them. Over time, the vertebrae grow together into one block.
why: For unstable or slipped vertebrae, a fracture, severe narrowing of the spinal canal, or curvature, when other treatment has not helped.
duration: surgery usually takes 2 to 5 hours, with 3 to 7 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you smoke. It slows fusion
Numbness or weakness in the legs, or bladder problems

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Back brace
prepare.text: Ask in advance if you will need a brace after surgery. It is sometimes fitted beforehand.

prepare.title: Home
prepare.text: Prepare your home: a high chair, and everything you need at waist height, so you bend less.

bring: A brace, if you were told to buy one
steps: You change, an IV line is placed, and stockings are put on to prevent clots
You are placed on your stomach or side
The surgeon makes a cut and frees the nerves, if needed
Screws are placed in the vertebrae and joined with rods
The position is checked on X-ray, and the wound is stitched
feel: Your back hurts for the first days and weeks. You will get painkillers
Old leg pain often goes faster than the pain from the wound
after: You usually get up in the first 1 to 2 days, with help
No bending, twisting, or heavy lifting. Your surgeon will say for how long
Walking is the best activity in the first weeks
The vertebrae take several months to fuse, checked with X-rays
red_flags: New weakness or numbness in the legs
You cannot pee, or cannot control urine or stool: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or pus from the wound
Calf pain, shortness of breath, or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.a: Not in the fused part, but the rest of the spine moves. Many people barely notice a difference.

faq.q: When can I sit and drive?
faq.a: Sitting a little, usually right away. Driving when your surgeon allows, often after a few weeks.

reminders.text: Spine surgery tomorrow. Bring your scans, brace, and documents. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
